available_assertion.statement: The local division quaternion algebra has the unramified quadratic cyclic model and unique maximal order, radical and quadratic residue field described in the cited theorem.
available_assertion.objects: The field and quaternion algebra in the fixed-type CJ comparison.
available_assertion.hypotheses: Nonarchimedean local field, its unramified quadratic extension and a uniformizer; current k=Q_q.
available_assertion.quantifiers: Every object satisfying precisely the stated source hypotheses.
available_assertion.parameter_range: Characteristic zero; the current global field is Q and the current local field is Q_q.
available_assertion.uniformity: Exact existence, identity or classification only; no quantitative estimate.
available_assertion.constants: Dimensions4 and2 where used; valuation factor1/2 in the local division case.
available_assertion.normalizations: Valuation is v(nrd)/2, not v(nrd); q is the actual inert prime, not the H19 prime3 specialization.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: Valuation is v(nrd)/2, not v(nrd); q is the actual inert prime, not the H19 prime3 specialization.
available_assertion.limit_order: No limits. Apply the source theorem before the following finite algebraic calculation.

specialization: Apply the generic nonarchimedean local division theorem at k=Q_ell0 to the already specified quaternion division algebra. Its unique maximal order modulo its radical is F_(ell0²). This supplies precisely the residue-field assertion at15748–15749.
boundaries: The incoming theorem is used through its generic available assertion, not its previous fixed-CJ needed assertion.
The count of residue embeddings follows from the degree-two finite-field extension. Lifting/classification of integral embedding orbits is not declared closed by this residue-field specialization.
The rank-one fractional-ideal and split Eichler lattice-pair assertions at15739–15747 remain separate.
